what: Pinned constants for deterministic GLSL emission, with provenance, and the polynomials built from them as executable data.
scope: Phase 0 covers the CONSTANTS and the POLYNOMIALS built from them, given exact inputs over the stated domain.

It does NOT cover the surrounding reduction: the Payne-Hanek-free argument reduction in det_sincos, the det_div inside det_log2 and det_atan, the Newton iterations in det_recip and det_sqrt, or the exponent assembly in det_exp2 and det_log2.

Those are whole-function properties and they belong to Phase 2, when the det library moves into the engine and can be emulated end to end. Saying so here so the record cannot be read as claiming more than it measured.

levels.1: provenance: every value names where it came from, in data rather than in a comment
levels.2: transcription: the value equals what that source says, re-derived by an independent implementation
levels.3: behaviour: the approximation built from those constants is measured over its whole admitted domain and its worst error asserted

UPSTREAM DRIFT, recorded and not reconciled: since 2026-08-24 atlas-darkroom gendetlib.py emits a FOUR-limb Cody-Waite split (PIO2_1..PIO2_4) with the low 15 bits of the first three zeroed, after Jason Davies, 'Accurate sin/cos/tan on Tenstorrent', 2026-02-23. Its first limb is 0x3FC90000, so cross_check_upstream reports a mismatch against this one. This record keeps the three-limb split it sealed and calls the four-limb form a prototype; adopting it moves bit patterns, which is an operator's decision. See docs/CONSTANTS-FINDINGS.md.

source.text: Cecil Hastings, Jr., assisted by Jeanne T. Hayward and James P. Wong, Jr., Approximations for Digital Computers, The RAND Corporation / Princeton University Press, 1955 - Part II, Sheet 11, page 135: coefficients C1 through C11 of the six-term odd arctan approximation on -1 <= X <= 1. It reached this record unattributed, through atlas-darkroom tools/determinism/gendetlib.py, whose comment reads 'atan - odd minimax on [0, 1]'
source.copy_checked: Sheet 11 read 2026-08-26 as page images from a scanned copy of the book (blasingame.engr.tamu.edu, P620 reference archive, PDF_Txt_Hst_Apr_Cmp_(1955).pdf); the scan has no text layer, so the coefficient block was transcribed off the page. Princeton Legacy Library reprint ISBN 978-0-691-65310-5
source.note: The attribution gap is closed: this set is Hastings 1955, Sheet 11, p. 135 - a 71-year-old RAND table, not a modern fit - and all six of its published eight-digit decimals round to the bit pattern above AND to its exact decimal, 6/6 on both fields. Hastings' range is -1 <= X <= 1, which for an odd polynomial is the [0, 1] atan_kernel sweeps. The obvious guess was ruled out at the source rather than from memory: cephes atanf.c is a four-term fit on [-tan(pi/8), tan(pi/8)] with an implicit leading 1, so it is not this set. 'minimax' is defensible but loose - the preface frames the work as best approximation in the sense of Chebyshev while also describing the investigation as numerical and empirical, so this is a graphically tuned Chebyshev fit and not a Remez computation carrying an optimality certificate - which is why the equioscillation test in verify-constants.py remains the load-bearing evidence, and this is the one kernel of the four that clears the float32 rounding floor (29x) and gets a verdict. `verified_against_source` stays false on purpose: level 1 reserves that flag for values level 2 re-derives on every run, which a fitted coefficient by definition is not, so the archival match is carried by this note and by docs/CONSTANTS-FINDINGS.md rather than by the flag.

AT0.note: UPSTREAM DRIFT, recorded and not reconciled: atlas-darkroom refitted atan for relative error on 2026-08-25, so gendetlib.py no longer carries AT0-AT5 at all - it emits ATQ0-ATQ7 for atan(r) = r + r*z*q(z), whose leading term is exactly r. cross_check_upstream therefore reports these six as fitted-with-no-upstream and the eight ATQ* as upstream-only. This record keeps the sealed set and does not adopt the refit: reconciling them moves bit patterns, which is an operator's decision, not a checker's. See docs/CONSTANTS-FINDINGS.md.

atanh_series.domain_note: s = (m-1)/(m+1) for m in (sqrt2/2, sqrt2], the mantissa fold in det_log2. NOTE the real det_log2 forms s with det_div, not exact division; this sweep feeds the series an exact s so the coefficients are measured alone.
atanh_series.series: truncated atanh, not a fit: the coefficients ARE 1/3, 1/5, 1/7, 1/9, so the error is a truncation tail and does NOT equioscillate. Checked as a series, not as a minimax.

atan_kernel.domain_note: r = min(|y|,|x|)/max(|y|,|x|) after the octant fold in det_atan, so r is in [0,1] by construction. As with atanh_series, the fold's det_div is not covered here.
